investigacion.base:
I couldn't get a live reading of the deflock.org counter, so there is no current figure from the resolution source itself. The one copy of the homepage the search returned is old: it showed **83,743 "LPRs mapped in the USA"** and 133 cities rejecting LPRs, 83,743 LPRs mapped in the USA. That snapshot is about 356 days old, so it is badly out of date. The number comes from crowdsourced OpenStreetMap data and goes up continuously.

**Recent figures (newest first)**
- **About 30 Sept 2026:** FindingFlock, which counts the same OpenStreetMap tags DeFlock uses, reported 143,301 cameras documented in the field by OpenStreetMap contributors and refreshed every six hours.
- **About 25 Aug 2026:** FlockHopper said DeFlock volunteers have mapped more than 130,000 ALPR cameras across the country.
- **Late July 2026:** Fox News said the open-source DeFlock map displayed about 119,000 readers across the United States. Flock Safety cameras account for about 83% of the mapped total.
- **17 Feb 2026:** NPR reported DeFlock had mapped the locations of more than 76,000 license plate readers across the country.
- **Past growth in OpenStreetMap counts:** January 2022 | 123 | January 2023 | 368 | January 2024 | 1,145 | January 2025 | 7,618 | January 2026 | 63,605 | July 2026 | 110,433.

**Growth rate**
- From February to late July 2026, the count rose about 43,000, or roughly 8,000–9,000 a month.
- From late July to late September, the gain was about 24,000 over two months, which is about 10,000–12,000 a month.
- In late July, DeFlock's own figure (about 119k) was a little above FindingFlock's July OpenStreetMap figure (110k). So DeFlock's counter may run slightly above third-party counts, or the gap may only reflect a difference in timing.

**What a straight-line projection gives (not a forecast)**
- Starting from about 143k on 30 Sept and adding 8,000–12,000 a month for about one month gives roughly **150,000–158,000** on 1 Nov 2026.

**Risks and caveats**
- A third-party site says DeFlock data includes 154,241 cameras documented and kept, including the 10,737 that came down. That means cameras get taken down, and it isn't clear whether DeFlock's counter includes or removes those. This could make the count go down or change how it's defined.
- The counter could drop if mappers clean up or remove duplicates. It could also lag if the site caches its numbers.
- Big bulk mapping efforts can cause sudden jumps.

**Before 1 Nov:** I found no scheduled events that would directly affect the count. Policy news, such as cities cancelling Flock contracts, mostly affects whether cameras are flagged as removed. I didn't find any prediction markets on this question.

**Sources:**
- [1](https://deflock.org/)
- [2](https://www.findingflock.com/stats)
- [3](https://dontgetflocked.com/)
- [4](https://www.foxnews.com/tech/license-plate-cameras-tracking-drivers-everywhere)
- [5](https://www.npr.org/2026/02/17/nx-s1-5612825/flock-contracts-canceled-immigration-survillance-concerns)
- [6](https://www.findingflock.com/learn/how-many-alpr-cameras-are-there)
- [7](https://deflocktheusa.com/tools/deflock/)

criterios: This question resolves as the number of LPRs mapped in the USA according to [DeFlock](https://deflock.org/) when accessed by Metaculus on or after November 1, 2026.
razonamientos:
(a) **Time left:** 24 days, from October 8 to November 1, 2026.

(b) **If nothing changed:** The latest reported comparable count would remain about **143,300 LPRs**. That is a third-party OpenStreetMap count, not a current reading of DeFlock’s counter.

(c) **If the trend continued:** Recent growth of roughly 8,000–12,000 per month points to about **152,000–156,000 LPRs** by November 1 on the third-party measure. I expect DeFlock’s displayed figure could be somewhat higher.

(d) **Experts and markets:** I found no expert numerical forecast or prediction market. Recent reporting describes rapid mapping growth but does not forecast a November count.

(e) **Unexpected low scenario:** A mapping cleanup, removal of duplicate or inactive cameras, or a stale site counter leaves the displayed count near **135,000 LPRs**.

(f) **Unexpected high scenario:** A large bulk-mapping effort pushes the displayed count above **190,000 LPRs**.

Percentile 20: 148000 LPRs  
Percentile 40: 155000 LPRs  
Percentile 60: 162000 LPRs  
Percentile 80: 174000 LPRs  
Percentile 90: 190000 LPRs

**(a) Time left:** About 3.5 weeks until 1 November 2026. The result is read from the DeFlock counter whenever Metaculus checks it on or after that date, so a short delay is possible.

**(b) If nothing changed:** The latest count is FindingFlock's figure of about 143,000 active cameras on 30 September. It uses the same OpenStreetMap data as DeFlock. The site that reported 154,241 documented, including 10,737 removed, gives about 143,500 active, which agrees. DeFlock's own counter may run somewhat higher: about 119,000 in late July against FindingFlock's 110,000 in July. So a frozen reading would be roughly 143,000–150,000.

**(c) If the current trend continued:** Mapping has added about 8,000–12,000 cameras a month, and the pace has been rising. Thirty-two days at that rate from 30 September gives about 152,000–157,000. If DeFlock's counter sits above FindingFlock's, it could reach about 160,000.

**(d) Experts and markets:** I found no prediction markets. The question creator's range is 130,000–220,000. Media figures (NPR, Fox, FlockHopper) are consistent with steady, fast growth.

**(e) Low-outcome scenario:** Mappers clean up duplicates or retag removed cameras and DeFlock stops counting them. Or the counter is cached or stale, or volunteer activity slows. Any of these could leave the count around 135,000–145,000.

**(f) High-outcome scenario:** A bulk import (for example from public records or a FOIA dataset) or a viral mapping campaign could push the count to 175,000 or more. Counting removed cameras would also raise it.

My median is about 155,000, with a wider tail on the high side because of possible bulk imports and differences in how DeFlock counts.
